To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the primer-dependent RNA chain elongation is possible with a synthetic template.

(a) the RNA polymerase initiates transcription at the 3'-terminal nucleotide unit, (b) the RNA polymerases of E. coli and T4 are able to synthesize RNA chains on a synthetic DNA template in vitro, (c) the RNA chains start with ATP and GTP, (d) the RNA polymerizes of E. coli are able to synthezise RNA on the 29-unit long DNA template, (e) the RNA product is heterogeneous,
(1) RNA chains initiated at the 5', 7' and 9' nucleotides of the template and (2) the primer was incorporated into the RNA chain and terminated at more than one position prior to the end
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the initiation process in transcription.
the synthesis of a synthetic 28-unit long deoxyribooligonucleotide.
the transcription of a 29-nucleotide unit long deoxypolynucleotide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the primer reaction with the deoxyribopolymer template was a complex process, the details of which are not understood.
a primer-dependent RNA synthesis was achieved with a 29-unit long synthetic deoxyribopolymucleotide as a template, but that the synthesis was limited to 20-25 nucleotides.
the RNA polymerase of E. coli can initiate the synthesis of RNA on the 29-unit long template, and can do so with a primer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a synthetic deoxyribopolymucleotide is a good substrate for DNA-dependent RNA polymerases, and the reaction can be controlled by the use of a primer.
a 29 nucleotide long deoxyribonucleotide can be transcribed by DNA-dependent RNA polymerases, and that initiation of the RNA chain can occur at more than one nucleotide unit of the template.
the RNA polymerase of E. coli can synthesize RNA chains of considerable length on a template as short as 29 nucleotide units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA-dependent RNA synthesis can be controlled by the use of primers.
the RNA chains synthesized in vitro on a synthetic template were initiated in a random manner and that the primer could not be used to control initiation.
the RNA polymerase of E. coli can initiate RNA synthesis on a short deoxyribopolymucleotide and that the site of initiation is determined by the sequence of the template.
